summary: This lesson plan is designed to help students develop their problem-solving skills by engaging in a citizen-officer deliberation roleplay. The students will take on civic roles and respond to a shared scenario, and then agree on a reasoned decision. The lesson will be facilitated by the teacher, who will circulate across the 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress. The expected output is a short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: The teacher will assess the students' understanding of the scenario and their ability to work together to reach a decision. The teacher will also provide feedback to the students on their participation and engagement in the roleplay.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: The students will reflect on their experience and what they learned from the roleplay. They will also discuss the importance of facing problems and finding creative solutions in real-life situations.
selected_activity:
Activity: Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency Level 8.5.2
Approach: Students use citizen-officer deliberation roleplay to explore 'Explains that facing problems is common, relevant to life.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 40 students using 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
